Crypto Firm Binance Covers 90% of Losses After $6.3bn Hack, FBI Points to North Korea

02 Nov 2026, 02:21 PM IST · GlobeWire Daily Editorial Desk · Source: www.bbc.com

Overview of the Security Breach

Binance, the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange, reported that it has covered 90% of the $6.3bn (£4.7bn) in digital assets stolen during a major security breach on Thursday. The company stated that sourcing the remaining 10% in the required amounts may take additional time. Binance has pledged to cover 100% of user losses from what is reported as the largest cryptocurrency hack on record, utilizing over $6.34bn in company funds and corporate treasury reserves.

Official Responses and Investigations

  • FBI Assessment: The Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) stated on Saturday that North Korea was responsible for the cyberattack. The agency reported tracking hackers converting stolen funds into Ethereum, anticipating further movement through decentralized finance and instant swap services.
  • Analytics and State-Backed Groups: Two analytics firms previously reported intelligence pointing to the North Korean state-backed Lazarus Group, also known as TraderTraitor, as the likely perpetrators.
  • Conflicting US Statements: US President Donald Trump stated on Saturday night that the US government remains unsure of the culprits, noting that officials are still learning about the incident.
  • Law Enforcement Action: The US Secret Service announced it is working continuously with private sector partners to trace, freeze, and recover the stolen funds. Binance confirmed that approximately $3bn in stolen assets had been frozen by Friday through collaboration with law enforcement and intelligence partners.

Impact on Users and Platform Status

  • Withdrawals: Binance announced on Sunday that withdrawals have been restored on several networks following temporary suspensions. The exchange previously indicated that withdrawal functions would resume in phased steps.
  • Covered Assets: The replenishment covers Bitcoin, Ethereum, Tether, and seven other widely-traded cryptocurrencies.
  • Breach Details: Initial investigations suggested an engineer's laptop was compromised, while subsequent updates revealed additional breach points. Co-Chief Executive Officer Richard Teng noted the attack involved multiple individuals and sophisticated methods, including a self-destruct mechanism.

Practical Implications and Verification

Users seeking official updates should monitor verified Binance communication channels and official statements from law enforcement agencies such as the FBI and US Secret Service. Claims regarding attribution and recovery totals remain subject to ongoing investigations.
